title: Probabilistic readiness gating + leaky-token load shedding to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Flapping readiness/liveness signals (from transient GC pauses, kernel preemption, and ephemeral IO spikes) are triggering rapid autoscaler scale-ups and scale-downs in certain regional pools. This behavior increases cost, destabilizes token-level latency SLOs, and causes cascading fallback traffic across regions. Existing approaches (longer probe windows, hysteresis) either increase time-to-detect real failures or still allow bursts of spurious scaling events.

Proposal: Implement a two-part mechanism: (1) probabilistic readiness gating — instead of a binary ready/unready on a single failed probe, compute a short-window probabilistic health score and expose a graded readiness signal to the router; (2) leaky-token load-shedding at the node/pool level — each node maintains a small token bucket used to accept degraded requests during soft failures, allowing graceful degradation without immediate removal from the target group. Together these reduce probe-induced autoscaler churn while preserving rapid detection for hard failures.

Key features:
- Short rolling health window (e.g., 30s) that aggregates probe outcomes, latency percentiles, and error-rate deltas into a single health score (0..100).
- Probabilistic gating: nodes with health score H accept new traffic with probability p = f(H) (e.g., linear mapping with a minimum floor) so routers gradually divert traffic away instead of all-or-nothing.
- Leaky-token acceptance: nodes can accept a bounded amount of degraded work (short-circuited tokens) while marking responses with a degradation header for telemetry and SLO accounting. Tokens refill slowly to avoid sustained overload.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler uses smoothed health-derived capacity signals and a rate limit on scale-up frequency. Scaling decision heuristics will weight token backlog and health score to avoid reacting to transient spikes.

Why this is different: instead of only tuning probe intervals/hysteresis (which we already have many tickets for), this introduces graded readiness and controlled degraded acceptance so that transient failures cause graceful capacity rebalancing rather than hard target removals and autoscaler thrash.
acceptance_criteria: During synthetic probe-flap test (30s noisy window) the autoscaler scale-up events/min are reduced by >=40% compared to current baseline
Platform 95th request latency under load stays within SLO threshold with <5% additional error budget burn during simulated node flapping
Region failover remains fast for hard failures (complete node blackout) with detection time <= 60s
Telemetry exposes token usage, health score distribution, and router acceptance probability; dashboards and alerts created
implementation_notes: Health score inputs: last N probe results, 1m latency p50/p95 deltas, recent 5xx count delta; map to 0..100 using calibrated weights
Router change: sampling-based selection using node acceptance probability; fallback to full routing if all nodes unhealthy
Node agent change: token bucket with configurable capacity and refill rate; token-consuming paths log degradation header and metric 'node.degraded.requests'
Autoscaler change: add health_score_weight and token_backlog_weight, implement cooldowns and max_scaleups_per_minute
Config surface: per-cluster tuning knobs under dedicated configs; defaults conservative for GA rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for health score computation and acceptance probability mapping
Integration test harness that replays historical probe traces and measures autoscaler events
Chaos experiment: introduce synthetic GC/IO pauses on subset of nodes and validate graceful diversion without mass target removal
Canary rollout to a single low-traffic region for 72h with synthetic load generator and observability checks
Load tests to measure cost delta and p95/p99 latency impact across steady and bursty workloads
rollback_plan: Remote-config feature-flag to disable probabilistic gating and token acceptance per-cluster
Router will read a flag and revert to binary ready/unready within 1 minute of flag flip
Autoscaler settings revert to pre-rollout hysteresis and scale-rate defaults
Post-rollback: run diagnostic job to surface any nodes that were in degraded state during rollout
